about: Pass 3 research for 104 runnable TTS/STT models that are thin, have no results, or sit in disconnected comparison sets (input: pass3-speech-input.json). Nothing in data/ was edited. Proposed comparison-only models are in `models`. Validated in a scratch copy: `node scripts/check.ts --validate-only` passes (1,294 models, 12,120 results, 781 benchmarks, 711 sources). Counts in `gaps` come from lib/score.ts toCells on that copy.

benchmarks.name: Paradee small-TTS comparison · 200 WikiText-103 sentences · UTMOS (utmos22_strong)
benchmarks.setup: Paradee report (arXiv:2610.06817v1) §5 and Table 3: each fixed-voice system reads the same 200 held-out English sentences (held out from a 12,000-sentence WikiText-103 corpus) in its own voice; naturalness predicted with UTMOS (utmos22_strong checkpoint), averaged over the 200 sentences. One author ran all systems.
benchmarks.display_unit: predicted MOS / 5; not human MOS, not accuracy
caveats: Automatic MOS predictor; the paper notes UTMOS missed an audible buzz artefact (§7, §9).
Each system uses a different voice (af_heart, lessac, Bella), so the score mixes voice and model quality.

benchmarks.name: Paradee small-TTS comparison · 200 WikiText-103 sentences · Whisper-base WER
benchmarks.setup: Same 200 held-out WikiText-103 sentences as paradee-wikitext200-utmos22; audio transcribed with Whisper (base) and compared with the source text (§5). WER % / 100.
caveats: Whisper base is a small ASR model; the paper says WER 'barely separates our models'.

benchmarks.name: carun tts-bench · 56-sentence English corpus · Whisper large-v3 WER
benchmarks.setup: carun/tts-bench (Apache-2.0): 56 English sentences in 7 categories (prose, numbers, acronyms, jargon, names, complex clauses, heteronyms) synthesised once per engine with its default/preset voice; each output transcribed by openai/whisper-large-v3 and scored against the input after the Whisper English normaliser on both sides; overall WER as printed in data/REPORT_DATA.md. The Parakeet-judge column is a correlated second ASR view of the same audio and is not recorded.
caveats: Small corpus (56 sentences, one seed); the author notes the heteronym category measures nothing.
Fixed-voice systems each use their own preset voice.

benchmarks.name: Wayu Thai TTS eval · English CER on 500 held-out LibriTTS lines (Whisper Large V3)
benchmarks.setup: Wayu/Paxa/Typhoon fixed-voice TTS report (arXiv:2609.03502v1) Table 8: each system synthesises 500 held-out LibriTTS English transcript lines with its Thai fixed/reference voice; audio transcribed with Whisper Large V3; mean CER in percent (divided by 100 here). Same evaluator and run as wayu-thai-cer500-typhoon-whisper.
caveats: Run by the makers of Wayu-Paxa-TTS-Edge, which was trained on LibriTTS transcripts (held-out lines are used for the test).
English intelligibility of Thai-voiced systems; complements the Thai CER of the same table rather than repeating it.

ledger.name: Paradee: Distilling Kokoro-82M into an 8M-Parameter Single-Voice TTS Model (arXiv:2610.06817v1), Table 3 small-model comparison
ledger.quote: arXiv abstract page for 2610.06817v1 links http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ and the HTML header states 'License: CC BY 4.0'. Table 3 caption: 'Paradee against other small open models on the same 200 held-out sentences, with the same scoring. ... Speed is real-time factor on one CPU thread of the same machine.' §5: 'All UTMOS scores are averages over the 200 held-out sentences.' 'Word error rate (WER) comes from transcribing the audio with Whisper (base)'. The single author ran every row.
ledger.attribution: Sahil Mahendrakar, 'Paradee: Distilling Kokoro-82M into an 8M-Parameter Single-Voice Text-to-Speech Model', arXiv:2610.06817v1 (2026), CC BY 4.0. Table 3 UTMOS and WER, UTMOS stored (x-1)/4 and WER % / 100. No endorsement.

ledger.reason: Same ESPnet repository and pinned commit b902372 (same Apache-2.0 LICENSE) as the existing LibriSpeech README match. The OWSM v3.1 README's 'Whisper medium (769M)' LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other cells are ESPnet's own runs of openai/whisper-medium (arXiv:2309.13876v3: 'we prepare all test data in ESPnet and evaluate Whisper in the same setup instead of reporting results from their paper'). Adding it to this evaluator puts whisper-medium in the same run as the 11 ESPnet LibriSpeech recipe checkpoints, linking that island to the main STT scale. The entry's scope text ('Only the ESPnet recipe authors' own WER tables, not third-party comparison numbers') would need one sentence added: ESPnet's own runs of public third-party checkpoints in ESPnet READMEs are in scope when the paper states ESPnet ran them. Only the Whisper medium LibriSpeech cells are used; OWSM v3/v3.1 are not catalogue models. Owner decision: this pools two ESPnet protocols (recipe beam search with LM vs greedy search with the Whisper normaliser) under one run level.
